question: Pipe P can fill (2)/(7) part of a tank in 18 hours, and pipe Q can fill (5)/(9) part of the same tank in 25 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 3 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 8 hours. Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:
solution:
**Given:**

Pipe P can fill (2)/(7) of the tank in 18 hours.

Pipe Q can fill (5)/(9) of the tank in 25 hours.

Pipes P and Q run for 3 hours, then Pipe R empties the water in 8 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Work done / Time taken

Time taken for full tank = Total work / Efficiency

**Calculation:**

Time taken by P to fill the whole tank

⇒ Time = dfrac{18 times 7}{2} = 63 hours

Time taken by Q to fill the whole tank

⇒ Time = dfrac{25 times 9}{5} = 45 hours

Efficiency of P, Q, R

Efficiency of P = (1)/(63)

Efficiency of Q = (1)/(45)

Work done by P + Q in 3 hours

⇒ Work = 3 × ((1)/(63) + (1)/(45))

⇒ Take LCM = 315

⇒ Work = 3 × (5 + 7)/(315) = (12)/(315)

⇒ Work = (36)/(315) = (12)/(105) = (4)/(35)

Pipe R empties this work in 8 hours

⇒ Efficiency of R = Emptying of (4)/(35) in 8 hours

⇒ Efficiency R = (-4)/(35 times 8) = (-1)/(70)

Combined efficiency of P + Q + R

Efficiency P = (1)/(63)

Efficiency Q = (1)/(45)

Efficiency R = (-1)/(70)

⇒ Combined efficiency = (1)/(63) + (1)/(45) - (1)/(70)

LCM = 630

⇒ Combined efficiency = (10 + 14 - 9)/(630) = (15)/(630) = (1)/(42)

Time taken to fill the tank when all run together

⇒ Time = (1)/(frac{1){42}} = 42 hours

**∴ Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in 42 hours.**
